#### Key Points

- Anthropic's shares are trading at approximately $1 trillion on secondary market platforms like Forge Global, surpassing OpenAI's $880 billion valuation[1](https://mlq.ai/news/anthropic-reaches-1-trillion-valuation-milestone-in-secondary-markets/# "Click to view source")
- The company's secondary market price represents a 163% premium over its $380 billion valuation from its February 2026 funding round[2](https://mlq.ai/news/anthropic-reaches-1-trillion-valuation-milestone-in-secondary-markets/# "Click to view source")
- Anthropic's annualized revenue grew 233% in a single quarter, jumping from $9 billion at the end of 2025 to $30 billion by March 2026, driven largely by coding tool demand[3](https://mlq.ai/news/anthropic-reaches-1-trillion-valuation-milestone-in-secondary-markets/# "Click to view source")
- On private stock marketplace Hiive, Anthropic shares surged 211% over three months while OpenAI shares rose only 8.5% in the same period[3](https://mlq.ai/news/anthropic-reaches-1-trillion-valuation-milestone-in-secondary-markets/# "Click to view source")
- Some investors are offering up to $1.15 trillion for Anthropic shares, reflecting intense competition for access to the company[1](https://mlq.ai/news/anthropic-reaches-1-trillion-valuation-milestone-in-secondary-markets/# "Click to view source")

![Anthropic Reaches $1 Trillion Valuation Milestone in Secondary Markets](https://mlq.ai/media/news_images/anthropic-1-trillion.png)

Anthropic's shares are trading at approximately $1 trillion on private secondary markets, surpassing rival OpenAI's $880 billion valuation amid intense investor demand. The surge reflects a dramatic 163% premium over the company's $380 billion valuation from its February 2026 funding round and signals a significant shift in investor sentiment within the artificial intelligence sector.[1](https://mlq.ai/news/anthropic-reaches-1-trillion-valuation-milestone-in-secondary-markets/# "Click to view source") [2](https://mlq.ai/news/anthropic-reaches-1-trillion-valuation-milestone-in-secondary-markets/# "Click to view source")

## Secondary Market Surge Reflects Investor Competition

Anthropic's valuation on Forge Global, a leading private marketplace exchange, now hovers around $1 trillion[1](https://mlq.ai/news/anthropic-reaches-1-trillion-valuation-milestone-in-secondary-markets/# "Click to view source"). This represents a substantial increase from OpenAI's $880 billion valuation on the same platform[1](https://mlq.ai/news/anthropic-reaches-1-trillion-valuation-milestone-in-secondary-markets/# "Click to view source"). The sharp divergence between the two companies reflects what investors without direct access are willing to pay for limited shares. Some Anthropic shareholders have recently offered to unload shares at valuations as high as $1.15 trillion, while one well-known growth fund reportedly offered to purchase shares at $1.05 trillion[1](https://mlq.ai/news/anthropic-reaches-1-trillion-valuation-milestone-in-secondary-markets/# "Click to view source") [2](https://mlq.ai/news/anthropic-reaches-1-trillion-valuation-milestone-in-secondary-markets/# "Click to view source"). This frantic bidding activity demonstrates the scarcity of available shares and the level of investor appetite for exposure to Anthropic.


## Revenue Growth Drives Market Confidence

Anthropic's annualized revenue jumped from $9 billion at the end of 2025 to $30 billion by March 2026—a 233% increase in a single quarter[3](https://mlq.ai/news/anthropic-reaches-1-trillion-valuation-milestone-in-secondary-markets/# "Click to view source"). The rapid revenue expansion is primarily driven by strong demand for the company's coding tools, which have gained significant traction among developers and enterprises[3](https://mlq.ai/news/anthropic-reaches-1-trillion-valuation-milestone-in-secondary-markets/# "Click to view source"). This operational performance has fueled investor confidence in the company's business model and growth trajectory. In contrast, OpenAI has faced slumping demand for its shares on secondary markets, with traders reporting decreased interest despite the company's higher valuation in recent funding rounds[1](https://mlq.ai/news/anthropic-reaches-1-trillion-valuation-milestone-in-secondary-markets/# "Click to view source").


## Secondary Market Pricing vs. Funding Round Valuations

The gap between Anthropic's secondary market valuation and its official funding round valuation is substantially larger than OpenAI's gap. Anthropic traded at $1 trillion on secondary markets compared to its $380 billion actual valuation from February 2026, a difference of $620 billion[2](https://mlq.ai/news/anthropic-reaches-1-trillion-valuation-milestone-in-secondary-markets/# "Click to view source"). By contrast, OpenAI's secondary market valuation of $880 billion is only $30 billion less than its $850 billion valuation[2](https://mlq.ai/news/anthropic-reaches-1-trillion-valuation-milestone-in-secondary-markets/# "Click to view source"). This disparity suggests that investors view Anthropic as having significantly more growth potential, or that speculative trading is driving secondary market prices to levels disconnected from official valuations. Share prices on the private marketplace Hiive illustrate this divergence, with Anthropic shares surging 211% over three months to approximately $900, while OpenAI shares rose only 8.5% to $608[3](https://mlq.ai/news/anthropic-reaches-1-trillion-valuation-milestone-in-secondary-markets/# "Click to view source").


## Market Dynamics and Share Scarcity

Those holding Anthropic shares are reportedly receiving multiple offers daily to sell their positions[1](https://mlq.ai/news/anthropic-reaches-1-trillion-valuation-milestone-in-secondary-markets/# "Click to view source"). The limited supply of available shares in secondary markets is fueling competition among buyers seeking exposure to the company. One Silicon Valley dealmaker even proposed trading his 14-acre estate for Anthropic shares, underscoring the intensity of demand[3](https://mlq.ai/news/anthropic-reaches-1-trillion-valuation-milestone-in-secondary-markets/# "Click to view source"). This supply constraint contrasts sharply with the broader investor appetite for AI-related investments, creating conditions where pricing on secondary markets can diverge significantly from official company valuations.


## Valuation Disconnect and Competitive Sentiment

The valuation gap between Anthropic's secondary market price and its official funding round reveals important dynamics about investor expectations and market sentiment in the AI sector. Anthropic's $1 trillion secondary market valuation against its $380 billion official valuation suggests investors believe the company's true value significantly exceeds what was established in formal negotiations with institutional investors. The 233% quarterly revenue growth provides some fundamental support for optimism, but the magnitude of the premium indicates speculative positioning rather than purely revenue-based valuation models. This contrasts with OpenAI, where the secondary market trades only slightly below official valuations, suggesting investors view OpenAI's pricing as already reflecting most available upside.

The stark difference in investor demand between Anthropic and OpenAI on secondary markets signals a potential revaluation of competitive positioning within the AI industry. OpenAI has faced slumping demand despite its higher official funding round valuation, while Anthropic shares are hotly contested among buyers. This shift could reflect confidence in Anthropic's technical direction, business model, or market execution—particularly around its coding tools—or it could indicate that investors perceive OpenAI as overvalued at its current secondary market price of $880 billion. The fact that shares trade at different prices on different platforms, with some offers reaching $1.15 trillion, suggests prices are still establishing themselves rather than reflecting deep consensus.


## Revenue Performance and Market Correction

The sustainability of Anthropic's secondary market valuation depends heavily on whether the company can meet or exceed the revenue and growth expectations already priced into the current market levels. Continued acceleration in revenue growth from coding tools and other products would provide fundamental support for these valuations, potentially normalizing the secondary market price closer to an official funding round. Conversely, if growth slows or revenue projections are missed, secondary market prices could compress significantly. The next major milestone will likely be Anthropic's next official funding round, which could either validate the secondary market pricing or create a correction if official valuations fall short of secondary market levels.

Investor behavior on secondary markets will also reflect broader trends in the AI sector and investor appetite for exposure to this rapidly evolving market. If investor demand for AI companies remains intense and capital continues flowing into the sector, secondary market premiums may persist. However, the extreme premium Anthropic commands relative to official valuations suggests limited room for prices to rise further without another official funding round that resets baseline valuations. Many investors holding shares at secondary market prices will likely be motivated to sell at or near current levels, potentially providing a supply wall that prevents further dramatic appreciation. The market will also watch whether OpenAI's secondary market valuation stabilizes or declines further, which could reshape investor perceptions of competitive positioning between the two companies.

# Anthropic launches staff share sale worth up to $6B: report

Feb 23  • 1 min read • Updated 20h ago

8

![](https://assets.msn.com/staticsb/statics/latest/views/icons/fluent/share_16_regular.svg)

![](https://assets.msn.com/staticsb/statics/latest/views/icons/fluent/more_horizontal_16_regular.svg)

![](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

Artificial intelligence company Anthropic ( [ANTHRO](https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/ANTHRO?feed_item_type=news&fr=1&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=msn.com "Anthropic")) is said to be offering some current and former employees the ability to sell shares in the company at a valuation of about $350 billion, allowing them to cash in at the level of a recent $30 billion fundraising.

The company has lined up $5 billion to $6 billion for the share sale, but the final amount will depend on how many eligible Anthropic employees opt to sell, _Bloomberg News_ reported on Tuesday. The details have not been finalized and could still change. The deal will be open to current and former employees who have worked at the company for at least 12 months, one of the sources said.

Anthropic’s ( [ANTHRO](https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/ANTHRO?feed_item_type=news&fr=1&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=msn.com "Anthropic")) latest funding round, completed earlier this month, valued the company at $380 billion post-money, including the cash investors put in. The company's investors include Nvidia ( [NVDA](https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/NVDA?feed_item_type=news&fr=1&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=msn.com "NVIDIA Corporation")), Microsoft ( [MSFT](https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/MSFT?feed_item_type=news&fr=1&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=msn.com "Microsoft Corporation")), Amazon ( [AMZN](https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/AMZN?feed_item_type=news&fr=1&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=msn.com "Amazon.com, Inc.")), and Google ( [GOOG](https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/GOOG?feed_item_type=news&fr=1&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=msn.com "Alphabet Inc.")).

OpenAI ( [OPENAI](https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/OPENAI?feed_item_type=news&fr=1&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=msn.com "OpenAI")), Anthropic’s biggest rival, has routinely done share sales, including a $6.6 billion secondary at a $500 billion valuation last year.

news.markdown:
#### Key Points

- Google to invest $10 billion immediately in Anthropic at $350 billion valuation, with $30 billion more if performance targets met[1](https://mlq.ai/news/google-invests-up-to-40-billion-in-anthropic-with-performance-based-funding-structure/# "Click to view source") [2](https://mlq.ai/news/google-invests-up-to-40-billion-in-anthropic-with-performance-based-funding-structure/# "Click to view source") [3](https://mlq.ai/news/google-invests-up-to-40-billion-in-anthropic-with-performance-based-funding-structure/# "Click to view source")
- Google Cloud providing 5 gigawatts of computing capacity over five years to Anthropic[1](https://mlq.ai/news/google-invests-up-to-40-billion-in-anthropic-with-performance-based-funding-structure/# "Click to view source") [2](https://mlq.ai/news/google-invests-up-to-40-billion-in-anthropic-with-performance-based-funding-structure/# "Click to view source") [3](https://mlq.ai/news/google-invests-up-to-40-billion-in-anthropic-with-performance-based-funding-structure/# "Click to view source")
- Follows Amazon's $5 billion investment in Anthropic earlier this week[1](https://mlq.ai/news/google-invests-up-to-40-billion-in-anthropic-with-performance-based-funding-structure/# "Click to view source") [3](https://mlq.ai/news/google-invests-up-to-40-billion-in-anthropic-with-performance-based-funding-structure/# "Click to view source") [4](https://mlq.ai/news/google-invests-up-to-40-billion-in-anthropic-with-performance-based-funding-structure/# "Click to view source")
- Anthropic valuation reached $800 billion or higher from investors; IPO eyed as early as October[2](https://mlq.ai/news/google-invests-up-to-40-billion-in-anthropic-with-performance-based-funding-structure/# "Click to view source") [3](https://mlq.ai/news/google-invests-up-to-40-billion-in-anthropic-with-performance-based-funding-structure/# "Click to view source")

![Google invests up to $40 billion in Anthropic with performance-based funding structure](https://mlq.ai/media/news_images/google-anthropic-40b.png)

Alphabet's Google has committed $10 billion in immediate cash to AI company Anthropic at a $350 billion valuation, with an additional $30 billion possible upon meeting performance milestones, alongside 5 gigawatts of Google Cloud computing capacity over five years[1](https://mlq.ai/news/google-invests-up-to-40-billion-in-anthropic-with-performance-based-funding-structure/# "Click to view source") [2](https://mlq.ai/news/google-invests-up-to-40-billion-in-anthropic-with-performance-based-funding-structure/# "Click to view source") [3](https://mlq.ai/news/google-invests-up-to-40-billion-in-anthropic-with-performance-based-funding-structure/# "Click to view source")[4](https://mlq.ai/news/google-invests-up-to-40-billion-in-anthropic-with-performance-based-funding-structure/# "Click to view source"). The deal follows Amazon's $5 billion investment in Anthropic announced earlier this week[1](https://mlq.ai/news/google-invests-up-to-40-billion-in-anthropic-with-performance-based-funding-structure/# "Click to view source") [3](https://mlq.ai/news/google-invests-up-to-40-billion-in-anthropic-with-performance-based-funding-structure/# "Click to view source").

## Investment Structure and Valuation

Google's investment includes an upfront $10 billion cash payment at Anthropic's $350 billion valuation, matching its February funding round level[1](https://mlq.ai/news/google-invests-up-to-40-billion-in-anthropic-with-performance-based-funding-structure/# "Click to view source") [2](https://mlq.ai/news/google-invests-up-to-40-billion-in-anthropic-with-performance-based-funding-structure/# "Click to view source") [3](https://mlq.ai/news/google-invests-up-to-40-billion-in-anthropic-with-performance-based-funding-structure/# "Click to view source")[4](https://mlq.ai/news/google-invests-up-to-40-billion-in-anthropic-with-performance-based-funding-structure/# "Click to view source"). An extra $30 billion would follow if Anthropic achieves specified performance targets, according to Anthropic statements[1](https://mlq.ai/news/google-invests-up-to-40-billion-in-anthropic-with-performance-based-funding-structure/# "Click to view source") [2](https://mlq.ai/news/google-invests-up-to-40-billion-in-anthropic-with-performance-based-funding-structure/# "Click to view source") [3](https://mlq.ai/news/google-invests-up-to-40-billion-in-anthropic-with-performance-based-funding-structure/# "Click to view source"). Investor valuations for Anthropic have since risen to $800 billion or more, with some secondary market estimates exceeding $1 trillion[2](https://mlq.ai/news/google-invests-up-to-40-billion-in-anthropic-with-performance-based-funding-structure/# "Click to view source") [3](https://mlq.ai/news/google-invests-up-to-40-billion-in-anthropic-with-performance-based-funding-structure/# "Click to view source").


## Compute Capacity Commitment

Google Cloud will supply 5 gigawatts of computing power to Anthropic over the next five years, starting in 2027, with options for expansion[1](https://mlq.ai/news/google-invests-up-to-40-billion-in-anthropic-with-performance-based-funding-structure/# "Click to view source") [2](https://mlq.ai/news/google-invests-up-to-40-billion-in-anthropic-with-performance-based-funding-structure/# "Click to view source"). This addresses Anthropic's compute shortages affecting its Claude AI service and supports significant infrastructure growth[2](https://mlq.ai/news/google-invests-up-to-40-billion-in-anthropic-with-performance-based-funding-structure/# "Click to view source"). The capacity leverages Google TPUs, noted for cost competitiveness against Nvidia chips[2](https://mlq.ai/news/google-invests-up-to-40-billion-in-anthropic-with-performance-based-funding-structure/# "Click to view source").


## Recent Funding Context

The Google deal builds on Amazon's $5 billion commitment to Anthropic this week, under which Anthropic plans to spend up to $100 billion on Amazon cloud capacity for around 5 gigawatts over time[1](https://mlq.ai/news/google-invests-up-to-40-billion-in-anthropic-with-performance-based-funding-structure/# "Click to view source") [3](https://mlq.ai/news/google-invests-up-to-40-billion-in-anthropic-with-performance-based-funding-structure/# "Click to view source"). Google joins Amazon and Microsoft as key backers in Anthropic's high-profile investor group[1](https://mlq.ai/news/google-invests-up-to-40-billion-in-anthropic-with-performance-based-funding-structure/# "Click to view source").


## IPO Plans

Anthropic is considering an initial public offering as early as October 2026[3](https://mlq.ai/news/google-invests-up-to-40-billion-in-anthropic-with-performance-based-funding-structure/# "Click to view source"). This comes amid rapid valuation growth following its $30 billion February raise that reached a $380 billion post-money valuation[2](https://mlq.ai/news/google-invests-up-to-40-billion-in-anthropic-with-performance-based-funding-structure/# "Click to view source").


## Strategic Compute and Valuation Alignment

The performance-based structure of Google's investment ties funding to Anthropic's ability to deliver on growth metrics, reducing risk for Google while aligning incentives for rapid scaling in a competitive AI landscape[1](https://mlq.ai/news/google-invests-up-to-40-billion-in-anthropic-with-performance-based-funding-structure/# "Click to view source") [2](https://mlq.ai/news/google-invests-up-to-40-billion-in-anthropic-with-performance-based-funding-structure/# "Click to view source") [3](https://mlq.ai/news/google-invests-up-to-40-billion-in-anthropic-with-performance-based-funding-structure/# "Click to view source"). By combining cash with substantial compute resources, Google not only deepens its stake in Anthropic's success but also positions Google Cloud as a critical infrastructure provider, potentially driving revenue amid pressures on its core advertising business from competitors like Meta[2](https://mlq.ai/news/google-invests-up-to-40-billion-in-anthropic-with-performance-based-funding-structure/# "Click to view source"). This multi-layered approach reflects broader industry dynamics where Big Tech firms back external AI developers despite in-house models like Gemini and Claude competing directly[1](https://mlq.ai/news/google-invests-up-to-40-billion-in-anthropic-with-performance-based-funding-structure/# "Click to view source") [4](https://mlq.ai/news/google-invests-up-to-40-billion-in-anthropic-with-performance-based-funding-structure/# "Click to view source").

Anthropic's appeal lies in its B2B leadership, contrasting OpenAI's consumer dominance with ChatGPT nearing one billion users[1](https://mlq.ai/news/google-invests-up-to-40-billion-in-anthropic-with-performance-based-funding-structure/# "Click to view source"). Google's bet diversifies its large language model strategy, hedging against rivals while securing preferential access to Anthropic's innovations through the partnership[2](https://mlq.ai/news/google-invests-up-to-40-billion-in-anthropic-with-performance-based-funding-structure/# "Click to view source"). The involvement of Google, Amazon, and Microsoft underscores a strategic consolidation among cloud giants to control AI infrastructure amid escalating compute demands[1](https://mlq.ai/news/google-invests-up-to-40-billion-in-anthropic-with-performance-based-funding-structure/# "Click to view source").


## IPO Timing and Compute Rollout

Anthropic's potential October IPO could capitalize on its soaring $800 billion-plus valuation, providing liquidity for early investors and funding further expansion, though market conditions and regulatory scrutiny will influence timing[2](https://mlq.ai/news/google-invests-up-to-40-billion-in-anthropic-with-performance-based-funding-structure/# "Click to view source") [3](https://mlq.ai/news/google-invests-up-to-40-billion-in-anthropic-with-performance-based-funding-structure/# "Click to view source"). The 5 gigawatts of Google Cloud capacity rolling out from 2027 will enable Anthropic to address current compute constraints on Claude, potentially accelerating model improvements and enterprise adoption[1](https://mlq.ai/news/google-invests-up-to-40-billion-in-anthropic-with-performance-based-funding-structure/# "Click to view source") [2](https://mlq.ai/news/google-invests-up-to-40-billion-in-anthropic-with-performance-based-funding-structure/# "Click to view source").

As performance milestones trigger the additional $30 billion, Anthropic's trajectory will hinge on meeting targets amid intensifying AI rivalry, with implications for cloud spending commitments to Google and Amazon totaling significant gigawatts[1](https://mlq.ai/news/google-invests-up-to-40-billion-in-anthropic-with-performance-based-funding-structure/# "Click to view source") [3](https://mlq.ai/news/google-invests-up-to-40-billion-in-anthropic-with-performance-based-funding-structure/# "Click to view source"). This could reshape B2B AI market shares, bolstering Google Cloud's growth while challenging OpenAI's position[1](https://mlq.ai/news/google-invests-up-to-40-billion-in-anthropic-with-performance-based-funding-structure/# "Click to view source") [2](https://mlq.ai/news/google-invests-up-to-40-billion-in-anthropic-with-performance-based-funding-structure/# "Click to view source"). Broader ecosystem shifts may follow, including heightened competition for AI talent and infrastructure.
